settings.title: They keep circling after they have lain down.
settings.text: A few turns before settling is just what dogs do. Turning, resettling, then shifting again ten minutes later usually means no position on that bed takes the weight off.

settings.title: They have started choosing the floor.
settings.text: Once foam has bottomed out, hard tiles genuinely are the firmer, flatter option. A dog picking the kitchen floor over their own bed has done the comparison and reached a conclusion.

settings.title: There's a dip that doesn't spring back.
settings.text: Press a flat hand into the middle where they lie. If you can feel the floor through it, so can their hips and elbows.

settings.heading: Three signs their bed has stopped working.
settings.note: A bed cannot undo ageing. What it can change is how much effort goes into lying down, and how much goes into getting back up.

settings.heading: Foam, not filling.
settings.body:
A lot of dog beds are filled with loose fibre or shredded offcuts. They can feel plump in the shop and still be flat by March, at which point your dog is sleeping on the floor with a cover over it.

Our orthopaedic beds are built on foam instead. On many of them, memory foam on top contours to hip and shoulder while a profiled egg-crate layer underneath spreads their weight, so it doesn't compress to the floor. Each product page says exactly how that bed is built.

The fibre-filled nest beds are made differently, and we say so on the page rather than letting you find out in month three.

settings.heading: Why they are named after fells and dales.
settings.body:
Borrowdale, Coniston, Grasmere, Windermere. The range takes its names from the places the walking gets done at weekends, which is also where most of the thinking about these beds happened.

Each one is built around a sleeping style rather than a price point. Curlers get walls. Sprawlers get surface. Old joints get foam that does not bottom out. Where a bed is fibre-filled rather than foam, the product page says so.
settings.places: Borrowdale, Coniston, Grasmere, Windermere, Kendal, Ambleside

settings.question: How do I know which size to get?
settings.answer: Measure nose to base of tail while they are lying down, then add 15–20cm. Where a dog falls between two sizes, go up: sprawlers need the length more than you would think. Every product page has a size guide built from that bed's own measurements, with breed examples.

settings.question: What's inside the orthopaedic beds? Isn't firmer better?
settings.answer:
Foam, rather than loose filling. Firmness is only how a bed feels on day one; what matters is whether it still holds them up a few winters on. Loose fibre shifts and packs down under a dog's weight, and foam keeps its shape far longer.

Many of the orthopaedic beds pair memory foam, which contours to hip and shoulder, with a profiled egg-crate layer underneath that spreads their weight. The fibre-filled nest beds are built for softness instead. Each product page says exactly what's inside that bed.

settings.question: Can I actually wash it?
settings.answer:
On most of the range, yes: properly, not just spot-clean. Most covers zip off and wash, following the care label sewn into each one, and selected beds have a waterproof inner liner that keeps wet coats, muddy paws and accidents away from the foam. Each product page says whether that bed has one.

One exception worth knowing before you buy: waterproof-fabric beds are wiped clean rather than washed with detergent, because detergent strips the coating off the fabric. Every product page says which applies.

settings.question: How quickly will it arrive?
settings.answer: Orders go out on working days, tracked from the moment they leave us. Order by [cutoff] on a dispatch day and it goes the same day; most then arrive within [delivery_min]–[delivery_max] working days. Tracking comes by email as soon as it's on its way.

settings.question: What does delivery cost?
settings.answer: Delivery is free on UK orders over [threshold]. Below that, the delivery charge is shown at checkout before you pay, so you always see it before you commit.

settings.question: What if my dog just won't use it?
settings.answer: Then it comes back. Let your dog sleep on it for up to [trial_nights] nights. [trial_terms] Just tell us inside that window. It doesn't need to be unused: send it back slept-on, hair and all. Full terms are in our [returns_policy].

settings.question: What does the [guarantee_years]-year guarantee cover?
settings.answer: The foam. Our orthopaedic memory foam beds carry a [guarantee_years]-year guarantee on the core, marked on each bed's page: if the foam loses its structure under normal use in that time, which is the failure that ends most dog beds, we'll replace it. Covers, zips and liners are wearing parts and sit outside it, and beds whose page doesn't mention the guarantee, such as the fibre-filled nest beds, aren't covered. Full terms are in our [returns_policy].

settings.question: Will it help a dog with arthritis or stiff hips?
settings.answer: A supportive bed spreads their weight so pressure isn't concentrated on hips, elbows and shoulders, which is what makes lying down and getting back up harder for a dog with joint wear. But a bed is not a treatment and it won't replace veterinary care, so please keep talking to your vet. What it can change is the surface they spend twelve to fourteen hours a day on.
